metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

evidence.quote: If you use LLM / "AI" tools for your contributions, please read and follow our _Generative AI / LLM Policy_
Only contribute code that you fully understand.

domains.suggested_improvement: state accountability holder for AI-assisted code
domains.reasoning: CONTRIBUTING.md names code contributions and requires contributors to fully understand any code they submit, implying human oversight of AI output, and points to a separate AI policy document (out of scope here) for the detailed rule. It does not itself state who is accountable for AI-assisted code beyond the general 'you must understand it' framing, so accountability is not explicitly named within this file.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting/notetaker bot use at all
domains.reasoning: The file contains no reference to meetings, recordings, or notetaker/meeting bots.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level or accountability for AI-generated docs/content
domains.reasoning: The Documentation section covers style rules (semantic newlines, docstring format, changelog conventions) but never mentions AI/LLM use for writing documentation, blogs, or other content assets.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of AI use in moderation actions
domains.reasoning: No text in this file discusses moderation actions (e.g., handling conduct issues, banning users) in relation to AI.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on AI use in reviewing PRs
domains.reasoning: The Governance section states 'everyone is welcome to review/merge pull requests of others but nobody is allowed to merge their own code,' but this is a human-governance rule about who may review, not a statement about AI performing or assisting review.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of autonomous/agentic AI activity
domains.reasoning: No language in the file discusses agentic or autonomous AI systems opening PRs, issues, or otherwise acting without direct human initiation.

domains.rationale_only_mention: Don't waste energy / tokens on something that we do not want.
domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on energy/resource use of AI tooling
domains.reasoning: The phrase 'energy / tokens' appears only as a colloquial reason to talk to maintainers before large contributions, cautioning against wasted effort/compute; it sets no rule, threshold, or accountability for environmental impact of AI use.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of infrastructure strain from AI activity
domains.reasoning: CI and test-suite requirements are discussed, but nothing ties AI use to server load, hardware cost, or infrastructure capacity concerns.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on use of project/user data for AI training
domains.reasoning: The file contains no discussion of whether contributor data, code, or discussions may be used to train AI models.

unscoped_statements.quote: If you use LLM / "AI" tools for your contributions, please read and follow our _Generative AI / LLM Policy_

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: CONTRIBUTING.md addresses AI use only in passing for code contributions - requiring contributors to fully understand any code they submit and deferring detailed rules to an external, out-of-scope AI policy document - while leaving notetaker bots, content, moderation, review, autonomous use, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and training-data use completely unaddressed within this file.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
